task:
In the captain transcript editor, add fuzzy retake detection that strikes the first copy of a phrase the speaker restarts, while keeping deliberate parallel clauses and stutters.

Create src/captain/retakes.py exposing find_retakes(transcript, *, sensitivity="balanced", min_pause=0.35) -> list[list[int]] and a cached helper _words_similar(a: str, b: str) -> bool. find_retakes reads spoken source order, ignores word indices already in transcript.removed, and returns non-overlapping groups of word indices (the false starts) sorted by first index. Support sensitivities "conservative", "balanced" and "aggressive"; an unknown name raises KeyError. A pause of at least min_pause between copies, or a long shared opening, makes detection more willing; chained restarts strike every copy but the last.

_words_similar compares normalized (case-insensitive) words: equality, one being a prefix of the other when the shorter word has at least 3 characters, or an edit distance of at most 1 when the shorter word has at least 4 characters. Empty strings are not similar. Do not strike single-word stutters, digit sequences, or candidates whose first copy contains sentence-ending punctuation other than an ellipsis. The second copy may add words, reword its tail, or follow a filler such as "um". Transcript.delete, _norm and _is_content_ngram already exist.

Add or update tests for the new behavior.
